patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Teams and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Microsoft Teams and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Microsoft Teams only if your buying job matches “M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on ” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than Microsoft Teams's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Teams leans shared coverage; OpenPhone leans business-phone, sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Teams and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Microsoft Teams is M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on — free Teams tier exists; Phone Standard ~$10/user; OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Teams (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Teams-leaning — vs OpenPhone-leaning business-phone, sales-calling.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Teams — Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story.

Limitations — Microsoft Teams: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; Teams Phone requires an eligible Teams/M365 licence plus PSTN (PAYG or Calling Plan); OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Teams is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job · OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · Avoid Microsoft Teams if you actually need OpenPhone's motion (Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
